text.title: mcp-gateway-composition Core Rules
text.summary: Migrated testable rules for mcp-gateway-composition. Verify and refine before relying on for production.

rule.statement: When you put an MCP gateway in front of multiple servers, pick exactly one composition pattern per agent: (a) virtual server — gateway exposes a curated subset of upstream tools as one logical server; (b) federation — gateways consume other gateways in a tree (used for org-wide rollouts); (c) per-client visibility — gateway filters the tool list by user/role/scope. Mixing patterns inside one gateway instance creates tool-list cycles and ambiguous deny rules.
rule.rationale: Each pattern has a different failure mode if applied to the wrong shape: virtual server breaks for hierarchical orgs (no nesting), federation breaks for end-user filtering (no per-call identity), per-client visibility breaks for static catalogs (overhead with no benefit). One pattern per gateway keeps deny rules unambiguous.

rule.statement: If an agent connects to more than 5 MCP servers OR sees more than 25 tools in its catalog, route through a gateway. Below those thresholds, connect directly. Measure tool count from the agent's perspective — sum of unique tools across all connected servers, after any client-side filtering.
rule.rationale: Tool selection accuracy degrades sharply past ~25 flat tools (Anthropic, Composio guidance). 6 average MCP servers × ~10 tools each crosses both thresholds simultaneously. The gateway lets you lazy-load toolkits and trim the catalog per client without rewriting upstream servers.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, servers_count is high-tier (above 10, the federation line this methodology's tree summary draws) and tools_total is advanced (above 25, the r2 selection cliff), the gateway-spec MUST set pattern to federation: a root gateway that consumes leaf gateways in a declared DAG whose config refuses to start on a cycle (fm-03), with the root doing federation only and every leaf gateway owning curation so that exposed_tools per agent client is at most 25 (fm-01) — no instance mixes patterns, per r1. namespace_prefix_strategy MUST be server-name prefixing on every tool (fm-02), auth_scheme MUST be centralised at the root with the caller's identity propagated on every forwarded call, rate_limit_rps MUST be enforced at the root per client, and role-tag resolution for visibility MUST live in one place with the deny path tested to return 403 (fm-04). audit.rule_refs cites r1 and r2.

rationale.source: Model Context Protocol specification (server composition and authorization); IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway documentation (virtual servers, federation); failure modes fm-01 to fm-04 of this methodology

rule.rationale: Past ten servers and twenty-five tools no single curated list serves every client, so the catalog has to be split across leaf gateways and the root only routes; letting the root also curate is the pattern mix r1 forbids and the source of ambiguous deny rules. Centralised auth and rate limiting at the root are what a gateway is for — pushed to the leaves they diverge, and fm-04's dropped filter is one refactor away.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, servers_count is high-tier (above 10) and tools_total is not advanced (at most 25, under the r2 cliff), the gateway-spec MUST set pattern to a single gateway — virtual-server when agent_clients_count is 1, per-client visibility when clients carry different role tags — and MUST NOT federate, because one layer suffices when the catalog already fits under the cliff and federation adds the cycle risk of fm-03 for no selection gain. exposed_tools MUST list every upstream tool with namespace_prefix_strategy set to server-name prefixing (fm-02), auth_scheme MUST be centralised at the gateway when shared_concerns includes auth and MAY pass upstream schemes through otherwise, and rate_limit_rps MUST be set at the gateway when shared_concerns includes rate limiting. audit.rule_refs cites r1 and r2.

rationale.source: Model Context Protocol specification; IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway documentation (virtual servers); failure modes fm-02 and fm-03 of this methodology

rule.rationale: Many small servers with a short combined catalog have a namespace and auth problem, not a selection problem: 'search' from two upstreams collides before any tool count matters. A single gateway with prefixing solves that; a federation tree solves a cliff this profile has not reached and brings a startup-cycle failure with it.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid and servers_count is low-tier — at least 5 (the Applies-If floor) and at most 10 — the gateway-spec MUST set pattern to virtual-server when agent_clients_count is 1 or to per-client visibility when clients carry different role tags, never federation; exposed_tools MUST be curated so the agent sees at most 25 tools (fm-01, the r2 cliff) with a CI count asserting it; namespace_prefix_strategy MUST be server-name prefixing (fm-02); auth_scheme MUST be centralised only when shared_concerns includes auth and rate_limit_rps set only when it includes rate limiting, otherwise both pass through unchanged. Adding a second gateway layer on this tier requires a rejected-alternatives entry naming the driver that forced it. audit.rule_refs cites r1 and r2.

rationale.source: Model Context Protocol specification; IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway documentation (virtual servers); rules r1 and r2 of this methodology

rule.rationale: Between five and ten servers the whole catalog fits one curated virtual server, and the 25-tool cut is the single decision that restores selection accuracy; everything else the gateway could do is optional plumbing driven by shared_concerns. Federation at this size is a second hop and a cycle risk (fm-03) with nothing to federate.
